content.thinking:
I'm planning the design of a Genshin-style lava golem in detail before writing the full file in one careful pass — a hunched, chunky basalt-plated monster with molten orange seams, gold filigree trim, and glowing eyes.

I'm now mapping out the skeleton structure, planning joint hierarchy from hips up through spine, neck, head, arms, and legs with coordinates, while being deliberate about using only the API functions I'm confident will typecheck cleanly without running the code first.

Adding jaw joint, then sizing the golem's head and shoulders proportionally—keeping the head small relative to broad shoulders, with overall height around 2.8m including back spikes. Now I'm sketching how to loft the torso body along the spine chain using elliptical radii at each station.

Since painted surfaces can't actually glow, I realize I need separate glowing elements like thin rods for the molten seams between plates, while keeping the basalt paint for crack texture with colors close to the emissive orange to make lit and unlit versions match reasonably well.

For the stone itself, I'm thinking hexagonal basalt columns — like Giant's Causeway formations — as a great motif for shoulders and fists, built from six-sided cylinder prisms bundled together, with flattened slabs for the plates. I'm defining the cel-shaded basalt palette with mottled dark purple-grey tones for the painted stone surfaces.

Shadows derive automatically from each point's lit color. Checking the paint budget: with a 1024 texel sheet and roughly 30-50 m² of golem surface area, I'm getting around 120-156 texels per meter, which gives acceptable 6-8mm resolution — bumping to a 2048 paint size within the 4096 atlas limit would sharpen the cel edges further. Baked normals get evaluated at build pose, which works fine, but I realize flat-color (non-painted) parts are capped at 64 colors and can't receive cel shading, so those need to use paints instead.

Most stone gets cel-painted, gold also gets cel treatment since paints don't count against the flat-color budget, and flat colors get reserved only for the handful of lava glow tones. Now I'm sketching out the part list, aiming for 300+ parts under the 1000 cap, using loops and helper functions to generate the hex prism geometry — considering whether cylinder segments below 12 shade flat or smooth, and whether the `flat: true` option still preserves UVs for painting.

I'm defining a rock helper that wraps part creation with flat shading, and deciding to always pass explicit bone references alongside position rather than relying on automatic nearest-joint weighting. Now I'm laying out the golem's skeleton coordinates — hips, knees, ankles — using polyline chains instead of splines so the stout legs don't overshoot their joints.

Still sketching leg/foot joints...

Counting toes: 3 per foot × 2 sides × 2 joints = 12 joints, and fingers at 2 joints each across thumb plus 3 big fingers per hand gives 8 per hand, 16 total. That puts the overall joint count around 60.

For the arms, I'm sketching a gorilla-like posture with shoulders, elbows, and wrists positioned so the fists hang low near knee height in a slightly extended rest pose, with fingers curling downward into the fist.

Mapping out the hand geometry with a palm block and tapered finger chains, positioning finger bases and tips, and setting up mirrored coordinates so the left and right arms reflect each other correctly.

Now I'm building the torso by stacking basalt pieces, sweeping a radius profile along the spine chain to form the core shape.

Shoulders sit at y 2.0 with widest chest point near 0.62 half-width, and arms positioned where pauldrons will cover the joint. For the core's surface, I'm writing a cracked lava-rock paint function with glowing orange crack colors using a cell-noise pattern to create the fracture lines.

I want the crack color to stay unshaded rather than darkened by the cel shading, so I'm nesting paints -- returning a basalt cel paint inside a conditional that checks for crack cells. I'm also planning to add a glowing lava-heart gem in the chest cavity with a gold ring, plus glowing seam rods between the larger plates to emphasize the molten theme.

For the chest glyph I want an original flame emblem design, not anything resembling existing game logos, with concentric gold rings around a glowing core. Now I'm defining a hex-plate helper function that extrudes a six-point outline with bevel into a flattened armor plate attached to a bone.

Working out the orientation math...

For irregular basalt-style plates, I'm jittering the hex outline radius with randomness for a faceted look, sized in meters. For mounting positions like on the chest, I'm figuring out the surface placement using an approximate ellipsoid for the chest and leaning toward a surface-sweep helper to position things around that curve.

Writing plate placement helper...

For hit.moved, I'm checking whether it returns a Frame versus just an offset Vector3 along the facing axis. Surface hits use azimuth/elevation coordinates around a center point, with azimuth 0 facing +Z and elevation 90 pointing up, and I need to handle the case where a hit returns null by skipping that plate. Analytical positioning could be more robust than relying on surface hits, but the hit-based approach adapts better to varying radii, so I'm leaning toward keeping it despite the fragility.

Now I'm sketching out the build order: colors and materials, skeleton rig, then the torso with its core sweep, plate armor on chest/back/abdomen with glowing seams, and a lava-heart gem set in a gold torus frame at the sternum. After that comes the shoulders — basalt-colored domed pauldrons topped with clustered hexagonal column spikes of varying height, gold-capped, with a magma ring at the joint.

Next I'm working through the arms — smooth cracked-skin sweeps from shoulder to wrist, hex-slab elbow guards, forearm bracers made of stacked flattened hex prisms with glowing gaps between them, and blocky fists with knuckle plates and obsidian claw tips. Then the legs follow the same logic: thick limb sweeps, hex-column kneecaps, glowing shin cracks, and wedge-shaped feet with toe columns. Finally I'm thinking through the head as a small angular basalt helm-block with a brow ridge and glowing eye details.

For the eyes themselves I'm deciding between decaling a glowing angular eye texture onto a skull part versus just building simpler extruded eye shapes — angular slits with an orange glowing rim and a smaller pale yellow glow inside for an anime-adjacent golem look. I'm leaning toward the extruded version since it's cheaper and more reliable than texture decaling.

Now I'm working out the jaw structure: a separate upper skull with a recessed mouth cavity glowing orange inside, and a swinging lower jaw block, with basalt cone teeth pointing up from the lower jaw and down from the upper. Then for the back, I'm planning a dorsal ridge of hexagonal basalt spike columns varying in height with glowing cracks at their bases, possibly with ash or smoke details.

I'm considering adding floating ember particles -- small glowing octahedra scattered around the golem's arms and back, attached loosely to the bone spine for an elemental effect, keeping the count modest (around 14) since they're technically floating parts. Then I'm thinking through gold filigree detailing -- torus/lathe bands at the wrists, ankles, and belt, plus possibly extruded gold swirl decals on the armor plates.

For the filigree itself, I'm weighing whether to use a textured plane with transparent cutout strokes laid over the chest, versus conforming decals applied directly onto the chest sweep surface -- but since plates would cover and clip that detail, I'm designing the chest instead with a large central breastplate slab bearing the gold filigree plane, flanked by pectoral pieces.

Designing SVG filigree texture...

I should also add tassel decals, like Genshin-style hanging tassels at the hips and shoulders—red-orange with gold knots, placed as angled card planes off the belt and pauldrons.

Since hanging cards render upside-down from downstream, I need to flip my drawing so the knot/attachment point ends up at the top when viewed correctly, and I should explicitly assign the bone (hips for belt tassels, shoulder joint for pauldron ones) rather than relying on auto nearest-joint detection.

I'm also tracking my glow color palette — distinct lava and hot tones for each glowing part — to keep the flat color count manageable, and reminding myself to write cleanly since there's no live typecheck until a separate repair pass.

Setting up imports and the palette definitions, using a toon shading helper with mottled base colors and automatic shadow derivation.

Still defining the palette...

I'm sketching teeth as pale pumice with warm highlights, then starting a crack-rendering function for the core that paints fractures onto a base color using a seed and scale.

Adding multi-band molten gradient colors to the cracks...

Now I'm pinning down exact body proportions: ground at y=0, feet topping at 0.3, hip joint around 1.22, chest centered near 1.95, shoulders at 2.1, head centered at 2.42 with top near 2.7, and pauldron spikes pushing total height to roughly 2.95m.

I'm also mapping out the spine chain path through three joints and realizing the round cap at the chest's end would overshoot the intended height by extending the dome too far upward -- so I need to either flatten the end cap or taper the radius near the tip to keep the silhouette under control.

Trying different end radii to get the dome height right: shrinking toward [0.5-0.6, 0.36-0.42] gets the chest/shoulder dome to around 2.1-2.45, which actually works well as a trapezius-like mass spanning roughly 1.2 units wide.

I'm reworking the overall height budget — spine end y, head center, and sunk head half-height — to land total figure height near 2.9 with the pauldron spikes included. I'll lock in hips at [0,1.2,0] with short legs as the base reference point.

Now I'm sketching the leg chain: hip, knee, ankle positions with a smooth radius taper from thigh to ankle, using a sweep with bone-specific fillet radii for the knee joint.

The round cap at the ankle end nearly reaches the floor, so I'm planning the foot as a separate low box (0.5 wide, 0.2 high, 0.7 long) positioned to overlap slightly below the ankle cap for a solid connection, then considering hexagonal basalt-slab shapes for the feet.

For the toes, I'll use short cylinder prisms (6-sided, radius 0.1, length 0.25) oriented along the z-axis and spaced across the front of the foot, possibly with gold toe caps matching the ankle rings.

Adding claw spikes at each toe tip with slightly reduced sides for a jagged look. Now moving to the arm structure, placing the shoulder joint and thinking through how to attach a shoulder pad relative to the chest ellipse dimensions.

Working out the arm chain for armL with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints, adjusting the sweep radii for a tapering gorilla-like limb and checking the wrist height so the fist hangs appropriately above the floor. I'm lengthening the arm proportions and repositioning the wrist and hand to get a more natural downward reach.

Now I'm designing the hand's finger structure, placing each finger base along the palm width and extending to tips angled downward and forward, using three joints per finger (base, mid, tip) for four finger chains per hand, totaling twelve joints per hand.

Still defining finger geometry...

I'm structuring the joint hierarchy next, planning how the wrist, fingers, and arm chains should parent to each other and figuring out the right way to reference the arm's tip joint for attachment.

Still working through the skeleton: naming spine joints with spine3 as the chain tip, setting parent relationships for arms off that spine joint, parenting legs to hips, and sketching out the neck and head joints with positions and aim directions so the head faces forward correctly.

I'm defining a jaw joint hinged near the back of the mouth, then designing the golem's blocky head as a flattened box or extruded prism shape to get that rough, hewn-stone look.

Finishing the profile outline, I realize the skull needs to hide the jaw, so rather than one perfect faceted silhouette, I'll build the head from separate pieces: an extruded cranium, a gold-trimmed brow ridge wedge, and cheek horns, placing the eyes just under the slanted brow front.

Still positioning eye geometry...

I'm positioning the eye at the slanted front face, computing where z lands along that linear profile so the eye sits at roughly z=0.29 with a thin 0.02 extrusion depth. I'm layering two glowing eye pieces — an orange outer at full scale and a smaller yellow inner offset slightly forward — both set to emit glow.

Now I'm adding facial detail: a gold-trimmed wedge brow ridge positioned above and in front of the head, plus a thin gold trim strip. For the horns, I'm sweeping a bezier curve from the sides of the head up and back, tapering radius from 0.07 to a pointed tip with hexagonal cross-section, aiming for an overall head height around 2.95 and considering gold-tipped color bands.

Still thinking through horn proportions...

Now I'm shifting to the jaw -- defining a lower jaw bone as an extruded profile below the skull, outlining its shape in relative coordinates against the head's top plane, with roughly 0.42 thickness before adding teeth.

I'm placing teeth: five conical lower teeth spiking upward along the jaw front, spaced evenly, and staggered upper teeth hanging down from the skull's front bottom edge. I'm double-checking the skull's bottom vertical range and reconciling the jaw's z-position with the skull geometry to keep everything aligned.

The jaw protrudes slightly forward past the skull like a bulldog underbite, which feels right for the golem. I'm adding a glow box between the teeth to simulate a glowing mouth interior, visible even when the jaw is mostly closed, and planning a slight resting jaw-open pose (around 10° on the x-axis) so the glow peeks through naturally.

Since posing a bone only affects its rotation while world transforms of parts built at explicit model coordinates stay fixed, I need to apply the jaw pose at the very end, after all jaw geometry is built, so everything attached to the jaw rotates together correctly. Now I'm figuring out where to place the glow plate so it shows through the gap between the jaw and skull underside once the mouth opens.

Placing the gullet glow box and a glow slab on the jaw top, sizing them so the opening gap at roughly a 10-degree jaw rotation reveals the glow convincingly. Then I'm sketching the neck as a short hexagonal prism between the head and chest, with a thin glowing ring at its base to mark the seam, and noting that a trapezius dome at the chest top will cover the neck's lower edge.

Now I'm working out the shoulder pauldron: a flattened dome sphere for the joint base painted with crack texture, topped by a cluster of roughly seven hexagonal columns of varying heights and outward tilt, and I'm defining directional vectors so each column radiates away from the shoulder center convincingly.

I'll generate 8 columns with evenly spaced azimuth and elevation angles tilting outward, positioning each at the dome surface and aiming them along their radial direction, then cap each with a smaller gold hex prism and finish with a glowing orange torus ring around the base of the cluster to suggest a magma seam.

Now I'm orienting that torus horizontally by mapping its geometry axis to match the vertical direction, then adding layered hex slab plates descending the shoulder's outer edge and hanging tassels from the pauldron's rim. For the upper arm, I'm defining a radius profile that tapers and bulges along the chain to give the limb a more natural musculature.

Still writing prism helper...

For bracers, I'm thinking hex prisms wrapped around the forearm, sized a bit larger than the arm radius for a heavy gauntlet look, rigidly attached to the elbow/wrist joints rather than bending with skin.

Mapping the arm joint chain: shoulder to elbow is one span, elbow to wrist the next, with wrist carrying the hand. For the elbow I'm adding a spiked guard — a hex slab plus a gold spike jutting backward with a glowing rim. For the hand, I'm sketching the palm as a hex prism oriented along the arm axis.

Now defining the palm as a flat box shape on the wrist bone, plus a backhand plate and a few small hex knuckle studs in gold rather than glowing. Keeping the hand open rather than fisted, fingers spread downward in a neutral pose, and now moving on to torso details with painted crack sweeps across the core.

For the belt, I'm working through a gold torus band around the waist, scaling it elliptically to flatten it slightly, and reasoning through how the aim direction and axis settings will orient the torus correctly around the spine bone.

I'm reworking the spine curve endpoint and estimating arc length to find the parameter t at waist height, then sketching a radius taper function for the torso barrel going from pelvis to chest.

I'm checking the chest geometry: the torso center sits around y≈1.7 with radius .42, putting the front surface near z=0.5 and the back near z=-0.34. Now I need to position the pectoral plates using azimuth angles around the torso, with 0 degrees facing straight forward.

Figuring out armor placement...

Adding honeycomb offset to alternating rows gives roughly 25 plates in front, similar coverage in back, with cracks showing through sides. Each hex extrude with bevel runs around 100 triangles, so ~60 plates total stays manageable at about 6k triangles — I'm now sizing plate radius and angular spacing against the chest's curvature so they sit properly on each hit normal without excessive overlap.

I'm coloring plates by hashing a random pick across a rock palette, then leaving a gap near the front center where I'll place a gold-framed gem centerpiece instead of plates, skipping hits in that azimuth/elevation window and placing the octahedral gem at the clear front-facing spot.

I'm building the gem's glow with an inner white-hot core, framing it with a flattened gold torus ring oriented to the surface normal, and layering a glowing rune-textured plane just behind it to bridge the gap where plates were skipped. Now I'm thinking about adding a lava crack glow in the torso belly between the belt and chest plates.

For the crack, I'm mapping clock angles around the torso tube to figure out where "front" actually is, since angle 0 corresponds to the back on a vertically running tube, meaning the belly front sits around 180 degrees, with lines at 150/180/210 landing there -- though those may get hidden under the chest plates.

I'm weighing whether to add thin glowing accent lines at the sides and front of the abdomen, sliced to just the lower torso region, against the risk of these sweep paths looking wiggly or unreliable since there's no way to verify the result before committing.

For the pelvis, I'm designing overlapping tasset plates hanging in front of the hips plus a gold belt buckle, positioning them using surface hits at a lower elevation angle near the pelvis center to get accurate placement coordinates.

Reworking the spine joint positions and radii so the chest barrel widens properly at the dome, with pectoral elevation angles placed to hit the upper front correctly given the new torso geometry.

Now I'm checking shoulder joint clearance against the dome surface, then setting waist belt height and hip joint placement so the pelvis sits properly on the legs with correct radii. I'm also laying out the dorsal ridge of hexagonal columns along the back, with elevation rows growing in size and a lateral pair of column rows flanking them.

Writing taper cylinder columns...

For arms and legs I'm planning hex-prism bands wrapped around the bone axis at intervals: upper arm gets two rings plus cracked skin texture and a shoulder pauldron, while legs get thigh rings, a knee guard slab, and shin plates -- all sharing a common `bands(bone, A, B, tList, rad)` helper. Now I'm setting up vector math utilities and closures within the build function to compute these positions concretely.

Writing hex outline and basis frame helpers...

Still writing plate function...

Writing column and cap geometry helpers...

Still writing imports...

Checking that Joint, frame, and offset are all correctly exported and typed for the skeleton and plate positioning logic.

Now I'm setting up metadata and defining the color palette for the lava golem — rock tones, obsidian, and gold shades using cel-shaded mottle textures.

Writing cracked lava paint function...

I'm defining varied crack intensities for core, arms, legs, and plates, then starting an SVG filigree texture with mirrored gold scroll strokes.

Designing a glowing rune ring with tick marks and tiny diamond glyphs, then moving to a tassel texture with a knot detail at the bottom.

Now I'm scattering glowing ember particles around the body using random angles and radii, keeping them clear of the torso and capping their height so nothing floats above the overall silhouette.

I'll skip adding ground rubble or lava puddles since this is just the creature itself, and start building out the actual builder code with the hips joint and spine chain.

Writing skeleton joints...

Adding neck, head, and jaw joints...

I'm planning to loop over left/right sides to build arms and legs symmetrically, storing each side's chain in a record, while keeping torso and head construction outside the loop since they're not side-dependent.

For the torso, I'm sweeping along the spine chain with a radius function and color, then adjusting the shift direction so the chest bulges forward rather than backward relative to the normal frame.

Now I'm creating a skin surface over the torso for hit-testing, and figuring out how plates near blended joint regions should inherit the nearest bone weight, picking chest or spine2 depending on elevation. Setting up a center point and preparing to loop through plates using the surface's around-point query.

Still defining plate rows and azimuths, excluding the central gem region where azimuth and elevation fall within a certain range.

Checking elevation at the torso belly: hits near y 1.3 conflict with the waist belt around y 1.4, so I'm separating the pelvis tasset plates from the belt zone to avoid overlap.

For the back I mirror the front az pattern with 180° offset, letting the spine columns sit embedded in the plates rather than skipping them. On the flanks between az 84-96 I'll leave the plates off entirely so the rib structure glows through as exposed molten seams.

Totaling around five rows and roughly 65 plates, each one gets lifted slightly off the hit normal with embedded thickness, colored by a weighted rock palette, and about a third get a small gold rivet stud added at the center for detail.

Now I'm placing a central gem feature at the core, using a guarded raycast hit to position it along its normal with an offset, then framing it with a hexagonal gold torus, a thinner outer ring, and a dark recessed disc beneath.

Then I add a glowing octahedron gem tinted warm amber, slightly stretched and lifted off the surface, plus a textured rune plane positioned just in front of it but still tucked behind the gold frame relative to the surrounding plates' height.

Now I'm also considering extra gold detailing around the chest—a collar torus at the neck base and a filigree harness strap sweeping across the torso to tie the design together.

I'm also working out a gold waist belt: positioning a torus around the spine at the appropriate height, scaling it elliptically to match the body's taper, and offsetting its center forward and in depth to hug the figure's curve correctly.

Then I'm adding a hexagonal buckle plate at the belt front, considering whether to make it solid gold or rock-colored with a gold filigree decal plane layered on top for detail.

Next I'm planning tasset plates hanging from the pelvis, five hex/trapezoid shapes spaced across the front arc below the belt line, positioning them along an elliptical curve matching the pelvis radius.

Still working out plate placement...

Still calculating collar geometry...

I'm skipping shoulder armor and backpack details for now, focusing on head decorations instead -- horns, brow ridge, cheek studs, and a gold circlet band positioned across the forehead of the cranium polygon.

Still placing the diadem...

Working through the cranium geometry: head center at [0, 2.52, 0.26], with the top reaching around y=2.76 (or 2.95 with horns/crystal), and the eyes sitting at roughly z=0.55 on the front plane. I need to check this lines up with the head resting on the chest dome at y=2.36.

Now defining the jaw outline relative to [0, 2.38, 0.26] with a set of z/y offset points, giving it a thickness of about 0.40 for the bone jaw. I'm adding basalt spike tusks on either side of the jaw pointing upward and outward, then planning lower teeth as a row of bone spikes along the jaw.

Working out upper teeth positioned on the skull with matching base, direction and length to interlock with the lower row. I'm also placing a glowing lava slab inside the mouth, mostly hidden, plus a dimmer hot-colored glow box inside the jaw interior.

Adding cracked paint texture to the cranium for glowing brow-vein fissures. Then I'm defining bezier-swept horns on each side with curved bases rising to sharp points capped under the height limit, using rock-colored bands fading to gold tips, six-sided and faceted rather than smooth.

I'm adding small hex-prism cheek columns pointing back-outward near the jaw, finished with gold caps, two per side. Now I'm setting up the pauldron and arm chains for each side symmetrically, defining shoulder-elbow-wrist joints as a polyline that will get a filleted corner at the elbow.

Working out the arm's taper radii — thicker at the shoulder, tapering through the elbow, bulging slightly for the forearm muscle, then narrowing again at a rounded wrist cap.

Now shaping the hand: positioning a flattened palm box slightly below the wrist, oriented along the arm's tilt axis, and reusing the cracked-paint rock texture for the palm surface since it's UV-independent.

Working out finger geometry next, defining base positions offset from the palm center so fingers spread outward symmetrically along the x-axis while their bases sit just below the palm's bottom edge.

Still defining joint chains...

Adding the gold knuckle ring and claw tip geometry...

Adding gold caps on the knuckle studs, then placing a hex plate with filigree detailing on the back of each hand, carefully positioning it relative to the palm surface. Now I'm moving on to designing the forearm bracers.

Working out the ring segments between the elbow and wrist, alternating rock-textured hex prisms with glowing gaps and a gold trim torus near the wrist, then setting up similar ring placements for the upper arm between the shoulder and elbow.

Now I'm designing the elbow detail: a hex guard plate angled outward from the back of the elbow, paired with a spike protruding along that same normal direction with gold-tipped bands, and moving on to building the pauldron's base dome shape positioned at the shoulder joint.

Still writing geometry...

Still placing geometry...

Shaping the leg geometry with tapered radii from thigh to ankle, then adding armor details: thigh ring prisms, a hexagonal knee shield with gold border, and a shin plate...

Working out the foot structure next: a flat bone shape for the ankle, a hex top plate with gold rim, and three toe digits each built from a two-joint chain with tapered radius and rounded caps...

Still writing toe chain code...

Now I'm skipping ground rubble details and planning a row of spine column bumps along the back, specifying their angular positions, elevations, and sizes down the torso.

For each column I'm computing its embedded base direction and offset, tapering radius with a hex prism and gold cap, plus a small glow ring embedded at the base for lighting. I'm double-checking the max height of the tallest back column against the torso's overall height limit to make sure nothing clips above 2.95.

Now I'm positioning scattered ember octahedra, computing angle and radius for each so they stay clear of the arms and body, constraining them to the back and side regions at larger radii.

Skipping drip glow under fists, no tail needed. I'll add gold tassel ornaments at the hip belt sides and front buckle, plus shoulder tassels, using frame-based card placement so they read as 3D from any angle.

Tassels won't get the glow treatment like the lava runes—only the glowing rune plane needs that shader. Now I'm working out the eye outline geometry, defining the inner and outer corner points so the eye shape reads correctly mirrored on each side of the face.

Working out the eye shape coordinates...

Checking the eye placement against the skull's half-width, I realize the outline extends past the edge if positioned too far out, so I'm shifting the x-origin inward to keep it within bounds. Now I'm adding a brow ridge wedge positioned above the eye socket.

I'm working out the rotation math for the brow box -- figuring out which axis and sign tilts the front edge downward so the ridge angles forward naturally over the eye.

Now I'm thinking about adding finer surface details: a thin gold trim strip along the brow, filigree decals on the pauldron plates and limbs, and gold glyph bands wrapping the ring prisms for extra texture.

I'm also tallying up the part counts roughly—plates, studs, columns, arm segments with rings and claws, legs—to make sure the total complexity stays manageable before finalizing the build.

Checking triangle budget: beveled hex plates run around 150 tris each times 65 plates, still comfortably under limits. I'm also double-checking variable naming to avoid collisions with the extrude function, confirming the jittered hex outlines stay non-self-intersecting, and verifying the bevel smoothing defaults are sane before moving on to gold paint detailing.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building parts: a `lava` wrapper that creates glowing flat-shaded geometry at a given joint and position, a `V` helper to normalize vector inputs, and a `prism` helper for generating tapered geometric shapes with configurable radii.

Writing column helper...

Now I'm checking the tile function signature and figuring out whether `Hit` is exported properly from the surface module.

I'll fix that typing mismatch later if it arises, using readonly for safety. I'm defining a weighted random rock-color picker function, then moving on to building the filigree SVG decoration.

Writing SVG code...

Building the rune circle...

Adjusting the circle radius to 22 so the gold frame hides it properly, then starting work on the tassel SVG...

Finishing the SVG and checking the orientation logic: the fringe strands converge at the knot and splay outward toward the top edge, matching how the card hangs upside down with the tip pointing downward.

Now building out the full lava golem: setting up the builder with a 2048 paint size, a seeded RNG, color palette for lava tones, and defining the skeleton structure before sweeping the torso shape with tapering radius functions along its spine.

Checking that these glow lines sit visibly between the belt and plate rows without being obscured, since they're just thin surface rods following straight paths.

Now I'm working through the tile placement logic, defining the center point and setting up alternating row offsets so each row's azimuth positions stagger against the one above it.

Still writing tile loop logic...

I'm checking edge cases—skipping tiles in the front-center chest gap, shrinking plate radius for steeper elevation angles, and verifying the belt torus doesn't overlap awkwardly with the lower belly row of tiles.

Now I'm setting up the pelvis plating: hoisting the chest ray-caster into a reusable variable, adding stud spheres offset along the surface normal, and defining pelvis tile rows at two elevation bands with staggered azimuth angles front and back, checking that the ray hits land at a reasonable height around the pelvis center.

Moving on to the belt and then the arms, I double-check a few type details—confirming that part colors accept string or paint fills, that glowing parts expose the mesh property needed, and nailing down the jaw bone pose so a forward-pointing bone tips downward correctly with its aim target slightly ahead and above the joint origin.

Next I'm making sure joint and chain names stay unique across the whole skeleton—hips, spine segments, neck, head, jaw, and the left/right shoulder joints—while chain names like "armL" can coexist since they aren't registered the same way. I'm verifying the spine chain builds from a catmull curve through the given points, the neck joint can take both an aim and an at parameter, and the finger spikes and horn bands use the correct signature with base point, tip or direction, radius, and color options, making sure band overrides don't conflict with the default color.

Now I'm defining the leg geometry, setting hip, knee, and ankle positions as arrays shared between the chain and the decorative rings, then writing a helper function that places a ring at a given interpolation point along a bone segment using a tapered prism shape.

Still writing leg decoration helpers...

I'm checking the gap spacing between rings along the forearm — realizing the ring heights and step intervals might be too close together to leave a visible gap, so I need to recompute the segment length to ensure proper spacing.

Now I'm working out thigh ring placement with spacing around .157 and height .1, giving a gap near .057 at t .46, then moving on to figure out shin ring positions between knee and ankle.

I'm defining a torus helper function for creating ring details on bones, then starting to build out the pauldron's dome and column geometry with sphere and torus shapes positioned relative to the shoulder bone.

Still writing column placement loop...

For the shoulder trim, I'll add a glow ring and a gold rim torus just below it to finish the pauldron detail, then move on to finalizing the full code.

I'm double-checking that all helper variables I've defined get used somewhere—the noise, mottle, cell, and paint functions for texturing, the offset for tile studs, frame for tassels, and the bezier/catmull curves for horns and spine. For the eyes, I need to make sure the extrusion has proper thickness, default orientation, head-bone attachment, and a flat color plus glow effect, matching the brow styling. Writing TypeScript for the outline scaling...

I'm adding a brow ridge box part attached to the head with rotation, then moving on to verify the chin and double-check that `rotation` and `scale` options are vector-based before writing the gold hex plate decal planes.

Writing sticker helper...

I'm reasoning through the sticker orientation so side plates stay upright using the world-up fallback, then wiring glow effects onto rune stickers through the existing texture material path. Finally I'm checking the floor contact math—making sure toe spheres, feet boxes, and legs all bottom out at y=0 so nothing clips through the ground.

I'm double-checking vertical clearances throughout the model: ankle caps meeting the leg sweep, finger/claw tips staying above the floor, and the tallest points (horn tips, pauldron columns, ember glow) topping out around y≈2.9. I'm renaming my sweep-sides array to avoid a naming collision with the `sides` option key before writing out the back column code in full.

Writing back column spec...

I'll default to null if the bone type doesn't match, fixing any compile errors later. For the Spot param on tile, I'll type the hit object with at, n, and bone fields, then just return b.root at the end.
